literal: The target the body is for suffering, knowing this, distress as helplessness will indeed not adopt the noble.
translation: Knowing that the body is but a target for suffering, the noble will not succumb to distress as if they are helpless.
modern: உடம்பு துன்பத்திற்கு இலக்கு என்று உணர்ந்து, உயர்ந்த குணமுடையவர்கள் துன்பம் வரும்போது கலக்கத்தை ஒரு வழியாகக் கொள்ள மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet explains how wise and noble people handle adversity. The body is naturally prone to physical and mental suffering; it is the very target ('இலக்கம்') at which suffering ('இடும்பை') aims. Knowing this fundamental truth, noble minds ('மேல்') do not allow distress ('கலக்கம்') to paralyze them or treat it as a state of helplessness ('கையாறு'). Instead of being overwhelmed, they accept adversity as a natural part of existence and maintain their composure.
